[Pixi](https://pixi.sh) is a package management tool for managing software environments and dependencies, similar to tools like Conda. We will use it to set up and manage the software environment needed for this workshop.

## Installation

To install Pixi on the Arrhenius cluster for you as a user, run the following command from any directory:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
```

This installs Pixi in the `.pixi` directory in your home directory.

Add the following lines to your `~/.bashrc` file to make Pixi available from any new shell session:

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/.pixi/bin:$PATH"
export PIXI_CACHE_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pixi-cache-$USER"
```

Start a new shell, or run `source ~/.bashrc`, and then verify the installation:

```sh
pixi --version
```

## Usage

The workshop environment has already been created, so you do not need to build it yourself.

### Interactive usage

To activate the workshop environment in an interactive session, run this command from any directory:

```sh
pixi shell --manifest-path {{< meta path_project >}}/apps/pixi.toml
```

This starts a new shell with access to the tools needed for the workshop. Run `exit` when you are finished to leave the Pixi shell.

### SLURM script usage

To activate the Pixi environment in a SLURM script, add the following lines before any analysis commands:

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/.pixi/bin:$PATH"
export PIXI_CACHE_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pixi-cache-$USER"
eval "$(pixi shell-hook --manifest-path {{< meta path_project >}}/apps/pixi.toml)"
```
